outcome: A visitor (Zach, an outside roboticist, the human behind a coding agent) lands on the robot-sdk site and can see what the SDK is, its packages by layer (viewers included), how they join on robot_msgs types, the real pick-and-place assembly, the agents that build the packages, and how to hand the skill to a coding agent; and can drill into the package and datatype graphs interactively to answer 'who uses this type, and is that declared and verified?'.
invariants: Only real data: site/data/graph.json (robot-sdk-graph/1), site/data/pick_and_place.json and site/media/*. The pick-and-place plant is simulated (MuJoCo) and says so.
graph.json is read at runtime (fetch, ?graph= override) with the build-time copy as the offline fallback; a regenerated file needs no code change.
React Flow (@xyflow/react 12.12.0) for every graph view, with show/hide and collapse/expand.
Every type edge carries kind (consumes/produces/imports), public, declared, verified and its file:line.
Viewer packages (role 'viewer', traj_compare) are first-class; agents build packages, packages never import agents.
Static, gh-pages hostable; the live site and gh-pages branch are untouched.
scenario: Answer: which packages touch JointTrajectory, which produce vs consume it, and is each use declared and lint-verified? Then: what does robot_controllers depend on, and how did the pick-and-place run assemble it?

axes.name: Graph role
values: the page itself, re-centred per type
a health map coloured by lint state

requirements.name: Relationships are legible and truthful
requirements.why: Zach's ask is the generated package and datatype graphs; their value is seeing exactly who imports a type, consumed vs produced, public, declared and verified, with no invented edges.
requirements.passCondition: From the site, the package-dependency graph and the type-use graph are both readable, and any single use shows kind, public, declared, verified and file:line.

anchors.1: One graph only, or edges lack kind/verification, or the picture needs the table to decode.
anchors.3: Both graphs exist; the use attributes are present but behind extra steps or hard to read at a glance.
anchors.5: Both graphs read at a glance; each use's kind, public, declared, verified and source line are one hover or click away.

requirements.name: Interactive focus answers the scenario fast
requirements.why: 'show/hide collapse/expand things as needed to see what you want' — the graph must shrink to the question.
requirements.passCondition: The JointTrajectory question is answered in three or fewer actions, and layers/groups can be collapsed and expanded.

anchors.3: Filtering works but takes several steps or loses context.
anchors.5: One or two actions isolate the type's producers and consumers; collapse/expand is direct and reversible.

requirements.name: First-minute understanding
requirements.why: It is still the landing page: an outsider should get what robot-sdk is, how to install it, and see real evidence (the pick-and-place run) without a tutorial.
requirements.passCondition: Above the fold: what it is, install, the layer idea; the real run is reachable in one step.

anchors.1: A tool surface with no explanation.
anchors.3: The pitch exists but competes with the machinery.
anchors.5: The pitch, install and a real result land in the first screen or two, and the graph supports rather than replaces them.

requirements.name: Required content is complete and findable
requirements.why: The new site must carry layers, viewers, both graphs, an Agents page, the pick-and-place example and the agent skill.
requirements.passCondition: Each of the six is present with real data and reachable from the first screen.

anchors.3: All present, one or two hard to find.
anchors.5: All six present, named in the navigation, each with real data.

requirements.name: Grows with the generated data and the commit
requirements.why: graph.json is regenerated by a linter lane and will grow (more packages, types, agents); 'landing page as a dashboard tied to the commit'.
requirements.passCondition: A swapped graph.json renders with no code change; layout survives about twice the packages; the data's generation time and source commits are shown.

anchors.3: Data-driven but crowded or breaks at 2x.
anchors.5: Data-driven layout that holds at 2x, and the commit/generation stamp is visible.

hardGates.name: Real data only
hardGates.why: No invented packages, types, edges or numbers; simulated things labelled.

hardGates.name: Reads graph.json at runtime
hardGates.why: The linter lane is replacing the seed; a swap must render with no code change.

hardGates.name: Static and isolated
hardGates.why: gh-pages hostable with no server code; nothing applied to the live site.

hardGates.name: React Flow graph views
hardGates.why: Zach's stated stack for the interactive graphs.
